body.x: TheDay1Lab (CEO Lee Jubong) participated in CES 2025, held in Las Vegas, USA, from January 7 to 10 (local time), as part of the KOTRA Pavilion.

TheDay1Lab is a startup with expertise in natural polymer research and development. With the introduction of the biomass-derived platform material 'RETARCH,' the company has drawn attention to presenting solutions to pressing issues such as plastic waste and microplastic pollution.

As a leader in the commercialization of natural polymers, TheDay1Lab began supplying its products to major domestic companies in 2024. The company explained that its products reduce customers' carbon emissions and advance ESG management practices.

The company aims to expand into diverse industries where the synergy of biodegradable materials can be maximized. At CES 2025, TheDay1Lab showcased its flagship RETARCH material to a global audience, emphasizing its potential as an alternative plastic.

RETARCH, developed from biomass sources such as starch and cellulose, is an eco-friendly material gaining attention as a new substitute for plastics. It is versatile enough to replace plastics in single-use containers, fashion and apparel, advanced semiconductors, and more.

body.cap: RETARCH was recognized with a CES Innovation Award in the Sustainability category last year | Provided by TheDay1Lab

body.x: RETARCH boasts many biodegradation conditions, including home and industrial composting, soil biodegradation, and anaerobic digestion. It is more effective than petroleum-based and eco-friendly materials at reducing carbon emissions. It decomposes without leaving behind heavy metals or microplastics, aligning with global carbon neutrality goals.

A TheDay1Lab representative stated, "After being recognized with a CES Innovation Award in the Sustainability category last year, we are reintroducing RETARCH at CES 2025 to expand our network with institutions and companies worldwide and validate its market potential. With growing global regulatory demand for ESG and sustainability, we are delighted to confirm strong interest in our biomass material."

The representative added, "To meet market demand and expectations, we plan to expand RETARCH-based mass production from its current focus on bags and injection-molded products, including mulching films and trays. This will allow us to cater to domestic and international farms and companies, driving further growth."

body.x: AVING News, which has covered CES for 20 consecutive years, continues to support the global ambitions of Korean SMEs and startups through various initiatives.

Before CES 2025, AVING hosted a series of Global Media Meetups featuring aspiring SMEs in Korea. The Meetups introduced Korean SMEs’ technologies, products, and services to media worldwide, expanding connections between the Korean industry and global media. Geekspin, Ubergizmo, Interesting Engineering, and Le Café du Geek participated in these meetups.
During CES 2025, AVING established the AVING Broadcasting Zone at The Venetian Hotel in Las Vegas, interviewing CES Innovation Award 2025 winners.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host a review conference with participating companies in Korea, offering them a platform to gain further recognition and enhance their corporate image.
